thread:
sam: Noticed onboarding quickstart mismatch: README curl uses REDWOOD_API_TOKEN but the sample Node app reads REDWOOD_API_KEY. New users copy/paste and get 401s.

leila: I hit this too. The sample app also prints a fake placeholder key in code which is a footgun. We should switch to process.env and add a short note on never committing keys.

omar: Can confirm reproduction steps: set REDWOOD_API_TOKEN, run node sample -> request header is empty -> server returns 401 -> SDK retries and client looks like it's hanging. Also Powershell copy/paste of curl fails due to quoting.

sam: Proposal: standardize on REDWOOD_API_KEY, update all language samples, and add explicit shell-labelled snippets for bash, zsh, and powershell. Also add a one-line on backoff so users know retries are expected.

doc-bot: created ticket DOC-908 "quickstart env var mismatch + powershell quoting" and assigned to @leila.

leila: I'll draft a tiny PR: replace placeholder key with process.env access, unify env var name, add PowerShell examples, and add a note about exponential backoff and retry limits. Will also add a CI check to grep for literal-looking keys (sk-.{10,}) in docs folder.

omar: For the curl examples, let's show both single-quote and double-quote variants and clearly label as "bash" and "powershell". Also add a tiny troubleshooting section: "If you see repeated 401s, verify your env var name and look for invisible characters (smart quotes) from editors."

sam: QA checklist for PR: 1) env var parity 2) shell-labelled blocks 3) replace literal key with env read 4) run quickstart test on mac/linux/windows runners 5) CI grep added.

leila: PR incoming in ~20m. pinging @eng-infra for windows runner smoke test.

ci-bot: linked PR 1123 to pipeline: docs-check, spellcheck, grep-secrets.

sam: thanks — should reduce a lot of sign-up support noise. :thumbsup:
